text: how could he have gotten through the yankee lines
interpretation_1: The speaker asks how he, rather than someone else, could have gotten through the Yankee lines.
context_before_1: Every other soldier was stopped. Somehow, this particular man succeeded.
context_after_1: His identity is what makes the escape so surprising.
interpretation_2: The speaker asks how he could have gotten through the Yankee lines, rather than some other lines or barrier.
context_before_2: The northern road was open, but the Yankee defenses were believed to be impassable.
context_after_2: The route through those defenses is what seems impossible.
linguistic_phenomenon: contrastive focus: subject vs path complement

text: the doctor wouldn't leave her people
interpretation_1: It was the doctor, rather than someone else, who would not leave her people.
context_before_1: The nurses and administrators had already abandoned the village. One person remained.
context_after_1: Her profession makes her decision especially significant.
interpretation_2: The doctor would not leave her people, although she might leave someone else.
context_before_2: The doctor had left the visiting officials, but she remained with the local community.
context_after_2: Her loyalty was specifically to the people she served.
linguistic_phenomenon: contrastive focus: subject vs possessive object

text: your husband killed louis palo for the money, where is it
interpretation_1: The speaker emphasizes that the husband killed Louis Palo, rather than merely threatening or injuring him.
context_before_1: We first thought your husband merely threatened Louis Palo. The evidence shows something worse.
context_after_1: The act itself was fatal, not merely intimidating.
interpretation_2: The speaker emphasizes that money, rather than another motive, was the reason for the killing.
context_before_2: We know your husband killed Louis Palo, but we are trying to establish his motive.
context_after_2: We believe the missing cash was the reason.
linguistic_phenomenon: contrastive focus: verb vs purpose adjunct

text: well, if that were true, that would put you out of a job, no
interpretation_1: The particular fact just mentioned, rather than something else, would put the listener out of a job.
context_before_1: Several rumors are harmless, but the allegation you just mentioned is different.
context_after_1: That specific claim threatens your position.
interpretation_2: The fact would put the listener, rather than someone else, out of a job.
context_before_2: The allegation would not affect the rest of us. Your position is the vulnerable one.
context_after_2: You are the person whose job is at risk.
linguistic_phenomenon: contrastive focus: demonstrative subject vs object pronoun

text: we ran away from violence
interpretation_1: The speakers ran away from violence rather than responding to it in some other way.
context_before_1: We did not confront the violence or remain where we were.
context_after_1: Leaving was the action we chose.
interpretation_2: The speakers ran away from violence rather than from some other danger or condition.
context_before_2: We were not escaping poverty or bad weather.
context_after_2: Violence was the danger that drove us away.
linguistic_phenomenon: contrastive focus: verb vs source complement

text: i'd like to ask you about the harvest festival
interpretation_1: The speaker wants to ask this listener, rather than someone else, about the harvest festival.
context_before_1: Several people attended the festival, but you were responsible for organizing it.
context_after_1: That is why I want your account rather than theirs.
interpretation_2: The speaker wants to ask about the harvest festival, rather than another event or subject.
context_before_2: I have questions about several upcoming events, but one is especially important.
context_after_2: That particular festival is the subject I want to discuss.
linguistic_phenomenon: contrastive focus: indirect object vs topic complement

text: to put things in perspective, you have to understand how mormons view the universe
interpretation_1: Understanding the Mormon perspective, rather than another group's perspective, is important.
context_before_1: Understanding other religions will not explain this particular issue.
context_after_1: The relevant perspective is specifically the Mormon one.
interpretation_2: Understanding the Mormon perspective is necessary, rather than merely helpful or optional.
context_before_2: It is not enough merely to glance at the Mormon perspective.
context_after_2: A proper understanding is necessary before the issue will make sense.
linguistic_phenomenon: contrastive focus: embedded subject vs modal necessity

text: so, i'll just monitor this newest g play gadget before offering it to my clients
interpretation_1: The speaker will monitor this particular gadget, rather than another one, before offering it to clients.
context_before_1: I have tested the older devices already. This newly released gadget is the remaining one.
context_after_1: It is the specific device I need to evaluate.
interpretation_2: The speaker will monitor the gadget before offering it, rather than after offering it.
context_before_2: I will not give an untested device to customers and evaluate it afterward.
context_after_2: The evaluation must happen prior to any client offering.
linguistic_phenomenon: contrastive focus: demonstrative determiner vs temporal adjunct

text: in my experience, its wi-fi is adroit from one environment to another
interpretation_1: The claim is based on the speaker's own experience, rather than someone else's experience or general evidence.
context_before_1: Other reviewers may have reached different conclusions, but I am reporting only what I observed.
context_after_1: The judgment is based specifically on my own experience.
interpretation_2: The speaker specifically considers the device's Wi-Fi, rather than another feature, adaptable across environments.
context_before_2: The screen and battery behave consistently everywhere. I am discussing the wireless connection.
context_after_2: That particular feature adapts well across settings.
linguistic_phenomenon: contrastive focus: possessive determiner vs subject noun

text: again, i urge all your listeners look at the transcript themselves
interpretation_1: The listeners should examine the transcript rather than relying on another source.
context_before_1: The recording and the summary leave out some important details.
context_after_1: The transcript is the most reliable source.
interpretation_2: The listeners should examine the transcript personally rather than relying on someone else to examine it for them.
context_before_2: A producer offered to review the transcript and tell everyone what it says.
context_after_2: Each listener should read it personally.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: information source (transcript) vs independent participation (themselves)

text: he was on the pot
interpretation_1: He, rather than another person, was on the pot.
context_before_1: I know someone was in the bathroom, but I thought it was his brother.
context_after_1: It was him, not his brother.
interpretation_2: He was on the pot earlier, but he is not there now.
context_before_2: You keep talking as though he is still in the bathroom.
context_after_2: He left several minutes ago.

text: he's with us at the table
interpretation_1: He is sitting with our group rather than with another group.
context_before_1: I thought he had joined the people from the other department.
context_after_1: No, he chose to sit with our group.
interpretation_2: He is at the table rather than somewhere else nearby.
context_before_2: I looked for him by the entrance and near the bar.
context_after_2: You will find him at the table.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: group affiliation (us) vs location (table)

text: i think that he'll definitely get his day in the sun
interpretation_1: The speaker is certain that he will eventually receive recognition.
context_before_1: You sound unsure whether he will ever receive the recognition he deserves.
context_after_1: There is no doubt in my mind.
interpretation_2: This is the speaker’s own prediction, although others may disagree.
context_before_2: Everyone else here thinks his career has already peaked.
context_after_2: They can make their own predictions.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: certainty (definitely) vs source of opinion (I think)

text: it was only - there was one salad in the supermarket
interpretation_1: The supermarket had only one salad rather than several.
context_before_1: I went in hoping to buy lunch for all three of us.
context_after_1: So I left it there and bought something else.
interpretation_2: The only salad available was at the supermarket rather than another shop.
context_before_2: The café, bakery, and corner shop were completely sold out.
context_after_2: That was the only place where I found one.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: quantity (one salad) vs location (supermarket)

text: little bit on the chin
interpretation_1: Only a small amount landed on the person’s chin.
context_before_1: Did the sauce spill all over his face?
context_after_1: The rest of him was completely clean.
interpretation_2: The small amount was on the chin rather than elsewhere.
context_before_2: I checked his shirt, his cheeks, and his forehead for sauce.
context_after_2: That was the only spot I needed to wipe.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: amount (little bit) vs location (chin)

text: no one seems to know the law in this state
interpretation_1: The law, rather than another subject, is what people do not understand.
context_before_1: Everyone understands the local customs and the usual procedures.
context_after_1: That is where all the confusion begins.
interpretation_2: The problem occurs in this state rather than in other states.
context_before_2: Officials across the border seem to understand the rules perfectly well.
context_after_2: Once you leave here, people handle these cases correctly.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: subject matter (the law) vs jurisdiction (this state)

text: peterson's the village spokesperson on the guard house issue
interpretation_1: Peterson handles the guard house issue rather than another local issue.
context_before_1: Maria answers questions about the school renovation and the new playground.
context_after_1: He can answer whatever you want to know about the dispute.
interpretation_2: Peterson represents the village rather than another organization.
context_before_2: The county has appointed its own representative for the meeting.
context_after_2: He does not speak for the regional government.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: issue (guard house issue) vs represented group (village)

text: swelling in her face, it dropped immediately
interpretation_1: The swelling affected her rather than another person.
context_before_1: Her mother showed no sign of a reaction, but the patient’s condition worried us.
context_after_1: No one else in the room developed any symptoms.
interpretation_2: The swelling decreased immediately rather than after a delay.
context_before_2: We expected the medication to take several hours to work.
context_after_2: We were surprised by the speed of the improvement.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: affected person (her) vs timing (immediately)

text: there's a lot of detail in that letter
interpretation_1: The letter contains a large amount of detail rather than a small amount.
context_before_1: I expected the message to be a short summary.
context_after_1: It took me nearly half an hour to read everything.
interpretation_2: That particular letter is detailed rather than the other letters.
context_before_2: The first two letters were vague and did not explain what happened.
context_after_2: Start with that one if you want the complete account.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: amount (a lot) vs document identity (that letter)

text: this is what we need to do in this country
interpretation_1: The action is needed in this country rather than somewhere else.
context_before_1: Other nations have already addressed the same problem successfully.
context_after_1: We cannot keep pretending that it is only their problem.
interpretation_2: We must take the action rather than expecting another group to do it.
context_before_2: We keep waiting for international organizations to solve the problem.
context_after_2: No one else is going to solve it for us.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: location (this country) vs responsible group (we)

text: we'll get to the delegates in a minute
interpretation_1: The delegates, rather than another group, will be discussed next.
context_before_1: We have already covered the organizers and the volunteers.
context_after_1: The support staff will have to wait until later.
interpretation_2: The delegates will be discussed shortly rather than immediately.
context_before_2: I know you want to discuss the delegates now.
context_after_2: Let me finish this point first.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: group (delegates) vs timing (in a minute)

text: best to keep bullies in their place, i say
interpretation_1: This is the speaker’s own opinion, although others may disagree.
context_before_1: The others think we should simply ignore this behavior.
context_after_1: They can speak for themselves, but that is my view.
interpretation_2: Bullies should be kept in their place, but other people should not be treated that way.
context_before_2: Should we be equally harsh with everyone?
context_after_2: People who behave respectfully deserve respect in return.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: opinion holder (I say) vs affected group (bullies)

text: everybody that counts is in this car right now
interpretation_1: Everyone considered important is present, even if some other people are absent.
context_before_1: Is absolutely everyone traveling with us?
context_after_1: The remaining people can follow in the other vehicles.
interpretation_2: The important people are in this car rather than another car.
context_before_2: Have the key people been divided among the different vehicles?
context_after_2: The other cars are carrying only the support staff.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: importance restriction (that counts) vs vehicle (this car)

text: guess you can put some cuffs on this young lady
interpretation_1: The young woman should be restrained rather than merely warned.
context_before_1: Are you planning to give her another warning and let her leave?
context_after_1: She is not walking away freely this time.
interpretation_2: The young woman should be restrained rather than the older woman nearby.
context_before_2: Both women were questioned, but only one of them committed the offense.
context_after_2: The older woman is free to go.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: action (cuffs) vs person (young lady)

text: i was at the doctor's
interpretation_1: The speaker, rather than someone else, was at the doctor’s office.
context_before_1: Which one of you went to the appointment yesterday?
context_after_1: Everyone else stayed at home.
interpretation_2: The speaker was at the doctor’s office rather than somewhere else.
context_before_2: We looked for you at work, at home, and at the pharmacy.
context_after_2: That is why nobody could find me.

text: i've never seen him get so emotionally involved in a case
interpretation_1: He, rather than another person, became unusually involved in the case.
context_before_1: Several members of the team were upset, but one person reacted much more strongly.
context_after_1: None of the others took it so personally.
interpretation_2: His involvement was emotional rather than merely professional.
context_before_2: He has worked hard on difficult cases before without taking them personally.
context_after_2: This time, the case clearly affected him.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: person (him) vs type of involvement (emotionally)

text: meanwhile, explain to me green carnations on a casket
interpretation_1: The surprising detail is that the carnations were green rather than another color.
context_before_1: White flowers would have made sense, and even red ones would not have surprised me.
context_after_1: Why would anyone choose that color?
interpretation_2: The green carnations on the casket require explanation, rather than those placed elsewhere.
context_before_2: I understand why there were green carnations in the entrance and reception area.
context_after_2: The flowers beside the body are what I cannot explain.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: color (green) vs location (on a casket)

text: not for nothing, but is better in her underwear
interpretation_1: She looks noticeably better rather than the same or worse.
context_before_1: You keep claiming that changing her clothes makes no difference.
context_after_1: That dress is clearly doing her no favors.
interpretation_2: She looks better in her underwear rather than in another outfit.
context_before_2: Which of those outfits actually suits her best?
context_after_2: The dress certainly is not helping.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: degree of comparison (better) vs clothing (underwear)

text: on the other side of the island
interpretation_1: The location is on the opposite side rather than this side.
context_before_1: Are they staying somewhere near us?
context_after_1: It will take hours to reach them from here.
interpretation_2: The location is across the island rather than across another geographical area.
context_before_2: Did they settle on the other side of the bay?
context_after_2: No, they are still on the same island as us.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: side (other side) vs geographical reference (island)

text: since you're a late addition, you're on my dime
interpretation_1: The speaker, rather than somebody else, will cover the listener’s expenses.
context_before_1: Who is paying for the extra person joining the trip?
context_after_1: Send all of your receipts directly to me.
interpretation_2: The listener’s expenses are covered by the speaker, but the other participants have separate funding.
context_before_2: Does your offer cover everyone joining the trip?
context_after_2: The original team members are covered by a separate grant.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: payer (my dime) vs person being funded (you)

text: there has never been a baby in my car
interpretation_1: A baby has never been in the car, although other passengers or objects have.
context_before_1: You may have seen child seats and bags in the back before.
context_after_1: Those belonged to relatives who borrowed the car.
interpretation_2: A baby has not been in the car at any time, not even once.
context_before_2: Are you saying a baby was in your car just one time?
context_after_2: Nothing like that has ever happened.

text: we got two more in an hour later
interpretation_1: Two additional people or items arrived rather than three.
context_before_1: We already had five, and I was expecting three more.
context_after_1: That brought the total to seven, not eight.
interpretation_2: The additional arrivals came an hour later rather than sooner.
context_before_2: Did the others arrive immediately behind you?
context_after_2: We had already been waiting for quite a while.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: quantity (two more) vs timing (an hour later)

text: we're in the middle of a homicide investigation
interpretation_1: The investigation concerns a homicide rather than another kind of offense.
context_before_1: Do you think this is just a routine traffic or property case?
context_after_1: Everything at this scene must be treated accordingly.
interpretation_2: Our group is conducting the investigation rather than another team.
context_before_2: Why are those detectives asking us to provide all the evidence?
context_after_2: Their unit is not responsible for this case.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: investigation type (homicide) vs investigating group (we)

text: you mean you got room in this motherfucker for a sink
interpretation_1: The surprising fact is that there is enough space for a sink, rather than merely enough money or equipment.
context_before_1: I knew you could afford the plumbing, but I thought the vehicle was far too cramped.
context_after_1: I never expected one would actually fit inside.
interpretation_2: There is room in this particular vehicle rather than only in another one.
context_before_2: I saw the sink installed in the larger truck, but this vehicle looks much smaller.
context_after_2: I thought only the other truck could hold one.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: available capacity (room) vs vehicle (this motherfucker)

text: you'll probably have to work on your dancing, though
interpretation_1: Dancing, rather than another ability, is what needs improvement.
context_before_1: Your singing and acting are already strong.
context_after_1: Your footwork is the weakest part of the performance.
interpretation_2: The need for improvement is likely but not yet certain.
context_before_2: Has the director definitely decided that you need extra dance training?
context_after_2: We will know after the next rehearsal.

text: at the mission he'd get a good education
interpretation_1: He would receive the education at the mission rather than somewhere else.
context_before_1: The local schools cannot offer him a place, and studying at home is not working.
context_after_1: It may be the best available place for him.
interpretation_2: The education would be good rather than merely adequate or poor.
context_before_2: I know the mission can accept him, but what is the quality of its teaching?
context_after_2: Their teachers have an excellent reputation.

text: he can be found in the eyes of a child
interpretation_1: Evidence of him can be seen in the eyes rather than in another feature.
context_before_1: Some people look for signs of him in a child’s words or smile.
context_after_1: That is where his presence becomes visible.
interpretation_2: Evidence of him can be seen specifically in a child rather than an adult.
context_before_2: You will not recognize him by studying the faces of powerful adults.
context_after_2: Children reveal the innocence you are looking for.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: body feature (eyes) vs person (child)

text: i'll get you one and meet you at the elevators
interpretation_1: The speaker will bring one item rather than several.
context_before_1: Would you mind bringing me two cups of coffee?
context_after_1: One is all I can carry with my bags.
interpretation_2: The meeting will happen at the elevators rather than somewhere else.
context_before_2: Should I wait for you in the lobby or by the front entrance?
context_after_2: Do not leave that area until I arrive.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: quantity (one) vs meeting location (elevators)

text: i'll put a tickle lock on my mouth
interpretation_1: The speaker will use a tickle lock rather than another kind of restraint.
context_before_1: A normal promise will not stop you from revealing the surprise.
context_after_1: This calls for a much sillier solution.
interpretation_2: The tickle lock will go on the speaker’s mouth rather than somewhere else.
context_before_2: Are you planning to put that strange lock on the box?
context_after_2: The box can stay exactly as it is.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: type of restraint (tickle lock) vs placement (mouth)

text: i'll see you in the park, same place
interpretation_1: The speaker will meet the listener rather than somebody else.
context_before_1: Should I send my brother to meet you tomorrow?
context_after_1: He does not need to come.
interpretation_2: The meeting will happen in the usual place rather than a different part of the park.
context_before_2: Should we meet near the fountain instead of our usual bench?
context_after_2: There is no reason to change our meeting point.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: person (you) vs repeated location (same place)

text: in a way, i'm kind of glad all this happened
interpretation_1: The speaker is only partly glad rather than completely glad.
context_before_1: You sound as though you are completely happy about everything that happened.
context_after_1: I still wish some parts had gone differently.
interpretation_2: The speaker feels glad rather than entirely upset about what happened.
context_before_2: After everything that went wrong, I assumed you regretted the whole experience.
context_after_2: Some good did come out of it.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: degree (kind of) vs emotional evaluation (glad)

text: the lady in the pub was very nice to me
interpretation_1: The woman, rather than another person in the pub, was kind.
context_before_1: Was it the bartender who helped you when you felt ill?
context_after_1: He ignored me the entire time.
interpretation_2: The woman was kind to the speaker rather than to somebody else.
context_before_2: She was rude to everyone else in our group.
context_after_2: I do not know why she treated me differently.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: person acting (lady) vs recipient (me)

text: there is someone in that room
interpretation_1: A person is in the room, despite the suggestion that it is empty.
context_before_1: You said the room was completely empty.
context_after_1: I can hear somebody moving behind the door.
interpretation_2: The person is in that particular room rather than another one.
context_before_2: Is the noise coming from the room beside the stairs?
context_after_2: No, it is coming from the room at the end of the hall.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: presence (someone) vs room identity (that room)

text: there's a human head in the bag
interpretation_1: The object in the bag is a human head rather than something less alarming.
context_before_1: You said the shape inside might be a mannequin part or an animal skull.
context_after_1: We need to call the police immediately.
interpretation_2: The human head is inside the bag rather than somewhere else.
context_before_2: We searched the box and the suitcase but found nothing unusual.
context_after_2: Do not open the remaining container.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: object identity (human head) vs container (bag)

text: yes, there's a flaw somewhere in the middle
interpretation_1: The problem is a flaw rather than a harmless or intentional feature.
context_before_1: You suggested that the strange section might be part of the design.
context_after_1: It was not supposed to appear in the finished version.
interpretation_2: The flaw is in the middle rather than near the beginning or end.
context_before_2: I checked the opening and closing sections but could not find the problem.
context_after_2: Focus your review on the central section.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: problem identity (flaw) vs location (in the middle)

text: i know what stands in the way
interpretation_1: The speaker knows rather than merely suspects what the obstacle is.
context_before_1: Are you only guessing about what is preventing the project from moving forward?
context_after_1: I have evidence that confirms it.
interpretation_2: The speaker knows exactly what the obstacle is, rather than knowing only that a problem exists.
context_before_2: We all know that something is blocking the project, but can anyone identify it?
context_after_2: The funding restriction is the problem.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: certainty (know) vs identity of the obstacle (what)

text: i wanna put you on the stand
interpretation_1: The speaker wants the listener, rather than another person, to testify.
context_before_1: Are you planning to call my colleague as your next witness?
context_after_1: She did not see enough to help the case.
interpretation_2: The speaker wants the listener to testify in court rather than take another role.
context_before_2: Do you want me to help investigate the case behind the scenes?
context_after_2: Your testimony would be more valuable.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: person (you) vs role or location (on the stand)

text: it's not like you're going on a crime spree
interpretation_1: The speaker rejects the idea that the listener is beginning a crime spree.
context_before_1: You are acting as though one bad decision will turn me into a career criminal.
context_after_1: One mistake does not mean that everything will spiral out of control.
interpretation_2: The listener is not beginning a crime spree, although they may be doing something else reckless.
context_before_2: Are you worried about a series of robberies or just one foolish trip?
context_after_2: The plan may be irresponsible, but it is not a series of crimes.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: denial (not) vs activity (crime spree)

text: mom put that in her book because it's interesting
interpretation_1: Mom, rather than somebody else, included the material.
context_before_1: Did the editor add that story during the final revision?
context_after_1: The editor actually wanted to remove it.
interpretation_2: Mom included the material in her book rather than somewhere else.
context_before_2: Did she put that story in the newspaper article she was writing?
context_after_2: The article contains a completely different example.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: person acting (Mom) vs destination (book)

text: noah decided to go at the last minute
interpretation_1: Noah, rather than somebody else, decided to go.
context_before_1: I heard that Emma changed her mind and joined the trip.
context_after_1: She stayed home in the end.
interpretation_2: Noah made the decision at the last minute rather than earlier.
context_before_2: Had Noah been planning to join the trip for several weeks?
context_after_2: Until that morning, he was certain that he would stay home.
linguistic_phenomenon: Contrastive focus: decision-maker (Noah) vs timing (at the last minute)

text: on the left side of the coffin, under the lid
interpretation_1: The location is on the left side rather than the right side.
context_before_1: Should I search the right side first?
context_after_1: You will need to reach across to find it.
interpretation_2: The location is inside the coffin rather than another nearby object.
context_before_2: Is it hidden inside the wooden chest beside the coffin?
context_after_2: Leave the chest alone and lift the lid instead.

text: sonny told me that he found you in the nursery
interpretation_1: Sonny found the listener in the nursery rather than somewhere else.
context_before_1: Did Sonny find you in the kitchen or upstairs?
context_after_1: He said you were standing beside the crib.
interpretation_2: Sonny told the speaker rather than somebody else.
context_before_2: I thought Sonny had told Michael where he found you.
context_after_2: Michael did not hear about it until later.

text: that's pretty damn heroic in my book
interpretation_1: That particular action is heroic rather than something else the person did.
context_before_1: Rescuing the child meant running directly into danger.
context_after_1: The earlier donation was generous, but it did not require the same courage.
interpretation_2: The speaker considers the action heroic, although others may disagree.
context_before_2: Everyone else here is calling the decision reckless.
